newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Gauze says African coffee plan won Brazil support.
newsitem.headline: Gauze says African coffee plan won Brazil support.

text.p: Ivorian Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze said on Wednesday African producers, supported by Colombia and Brazil, would push for a cut in coffee exports at a producer meeting in Brazil next week.
In a speech at the Asia Coffee Conference here, Gauze said there could be an excess of 2.5 million to 3.0 million 60-kg bags of coffee in the first half of 1997.
"The African group, supported by Colombia and Brazil, will take steps to see the situation normalise," said Gauze, who is also head of the InterAfrican Coffee Organisation.
"In general the idea is to reduce the volume of coffee exported by the ACPC member countries in the period of January to June 1997 from 26.3 million to 23.7 million bags," he said.
The Brazilian government has so far declined to comment on whether ACPC exports needed to be cut but did support the African call for an emergency ACPC session.
But Colombia has said it agreed with the African producers on the need to cut exports by ACPC members by a further 2.5 million bags in the first half of this year.
Brazil and Colombia are the world's top two coffee exporters. ACPC members are to meet for an emergency session in Brazilian city of Rio de Janeiro on January 23.

ACPC officials have said the meeting would analyse the market situation, assess the implementation of the export programme in the first six months from June to December 1996 and decide whether to alter the export quotas.
